description: The full data science workflow on real datasets: collecting and cleaning data, warehousing and business intelligence, visualisation, machine learning for clustering, dimensionality reduction, association rules, regression and classification, big data tools, and the ethics and storytelling that make results usable. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory data science course.
modelledOn: Adhikari, DeNero and Wagner, Computational and Inferential Thinking: The Foundations of Data Science
Wickham, Cetinkaya-Rundel and Grolemund, R for Data Science
Provost and Fawcett, Data Science for Business
outcomes: Describe the data science life cycle and plan a project from question to deployed insight.
Use Python and R to load, clean, transform, blend and summarise data from files, databases, APIs and the web.
Design a simple data warehouse and build business intelligence dashboards.
Create honest, effective visualisations and communicate findings as a data story.
Apply clustering, PCA, association rules, regression and classification with proper validation.
Process data at scale with distributed tools and handle privacy and ethics responsibly.

units.title: Introduction to data science and the project life cycle
topics: What data science is: statistics, computing and domain knowledge; roles in a data team
The life cycle: question, acquire, clean, explore, model, evaluate, communicate, deploy, monitor (CRISP-DM)
Data types and sources: structured, semi-structured, unstructured; open data from the Ghana Statistical Service and the World Bank
Framing business and research questions; defining success metrics
Reproducible work: notebooks, scripts, version control, environments

units.title: R and Python for data
topics: Python: NumPy arrays, pandas DataFrames, indexing, grouping, merging, reshaping
R: vectors, data frames, the tidyverse (dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2)
Reading and writing CSV, Excel, JSON, SQL; dates and times; text and regular expressions
Exploratory data analysis: summaries, distributions, outliers, missing data
Choosing between R and Python and moving between them

units.title: Data collection and blending
topics: Collecting data: surveys, sensors, logs, APIs, web scraping (ethically and legally)
Data cleaning: types, duplicates, inconsistent categories, missing values and imputation, outliers
Blending sources: joins, entity resolution, fuzzy matching, unit and currency harmonisation
Data quality assessment and documentation (data dictionaries, provenance)

units.title: Business intelligence and data warehousing
topics: OLTP versus OLAP; the data warehouse and data marts; ETL and ELT pipelines
Dimensional modelling: facts, dimensions, star and snowflake schemas
OLAP operations: slice, dice, roll-up, drill-down; SQL for analytics (window functions, CUBE)
Dashboards with Power BI, Tableau, Metabase or Superset; KPIs for a retail chain or a hospital

units.title: Data visualisation
topics: Principles: encoding, chart choice, colour, scales, small multiples, avoiding deception
matplotlib, seaborn, plotly and ggplot2; maps and geospatial plots of Ghana's regions
Interactive dashboards and notebooks
Critiquing charts from the press and government reports

units.title: Machine learning: regression and classification
topics: Supervised learning setup; train/validation/test splits; cross-validation; overfitting and regularisation
Linear and polynomial regression; logistic regression; k-nearest neighbours; decision trees and random forests; gradient boosting
Evaluation: RMSE, R-squared, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, confusion matrices, class imbalance
Feature engineering, encoding, scaling, pipelines in scikit-learn and tidymodels
Case: predicting loan default, crop yield or student dropout

units.title: Machine learning: clustering, PCA and association rules
topics: k-means, hierarchical and DBSCAN clustering; choosing k; interpreting clusters (customer segmentation)
Principal component analysis: variance, loadings, visualisation of high-dimensional data; t-SNE and UMAP in brief
Association rules: support, confidence, lift, Apriori and FP-growth; market basket analysis
Anomaly detection basics

units.title: Big data analytics
topics: The Vs of big data; when a laptop is not enough
Distributed storage and compute: HDFS, MapReduce, Spark DataFrames and MLlib; cloud data warehouses
Streaming analytics and real-time dashboards
Working with big data on a small budget: sampling, columnar formats (Parquet), DuckDB

units.title: Ethics, privacy and storytelling with data
topics: Privacy, consent, anonymisation and re-identification; Ghana's Data Protection Act and GDPR
Bias in data and models; fairness metrics; algorithmic accountability; responsible AI
Storytelling: narrative structure, audience, executive summaries, presenting uncertainty
Capstone: an end-to-end project on a local dataset with a dashboard, model and written story
